rationale: Round 1 compiled and ran correctly with no ICE, so this table raises security/diversity pressure across all seven passes while keeping cost weights tuned to RealMM's profile: the program is tiny (903 text bytes, 7 functions) so absolute size growth from SUB/BCF/SPLIT is cheap, but execution is dominated by the hot Mm matrix-multiply triple loop, so BCF (loop-body bloat executed per iteration) and ICALL/IBR (indirection on the inner-product hot path) get only moderate RuntimeCost weights relative to their security gains to avoid stacking heavy dispatch overhead onto the hottest function. SUB is pushed highest since it is nearly free at runtime and compounds with every other pass; FLA and SPLIT get strong weights to destroy the recognizable structured loop nest and basic-block layout of Mm/rInnerproduct, which are the primary reverse-engineering anchors; IGV stays mid-range because the program has few globals and its size cost grows fastest on a 903-byte baseline; correctness-risk weights remain low across the board given the clean round-1 result, allowing the selector to apply passes more aggressively wherever per-function features favor them.
